answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a refundable stake before it may bid, then slash that stake when independent audits show the identity reused another agent’s credentials or fabricated completed work. Rewards accrue only after a delayed challenge window, so a plume of hollow accounts cannot cheaply harvest payouts and disappear before review. An attacker must fund every umber identity separately and keep that capital exposed long enough for detection, making large-scale Sybil attacks costly even when account creation is free.
